dataflow.summary: Unauthenticated WebSocket -> register -> bounded frame validation -> broadcast to all peers.

attackPath.impact: Relay availability degradation and unsolicited encrypted traffic to connected clients.

reachability.summary: Reachable whenever a public relay endpoint is deployed; no public deployment was available in this workspace.

codeEvidence.code: if not await self.register(websocket): ... await self.broadcast(websocket, message)
codeEvidence.explanation: A connected client is registered and later broadcast is gated only by frame shape and rate limits.
codeEvidence.label: Connection registration

codeEvidence.explanation: All clients enter one global room; no identity or access proof is checked.
codeEvidence.label: Global room admission

confidence.rationale: The connection handlers have no authentication or authorization check before registration and broadcast.

findings.remediation: Add an authenticated admission mechanism that does not expose message keys, such as a short-lived relay access token issued by the service or a proof-of-possession handshake bound to the node signing key. Keep the existing client, payload, per-client rate, and connection limits as defense in depth; add abuse monitoring and per-IP/account quotas at the edge.

rootCause.summary: Relay admission is modeled as transport connectivity rather than authenticated membership.

severity.rationale: An internet-reachable deployment allows unaffiliated clients to consume connection capacity and send bounded frames to every connected client. End-to-end encryption limits plaintext exposure, but availability and traffic integrity remain affected.

findings.summary: Both relay implementations accept a WebSocket connection and broadcast protocol-shaped frames without authenticating the connecting node or proving possession of a MeshGram identity.
findings.title: Relay accepts arbitrary clients without admission authentication

validation.counterevidence_or_proof_gap: Message signatures and recipient-side decryption reduce content forgery, and bounded client/rate/payload limits reduce but do not remove service abuse.
validation.method: Source trace of both server entrypoints and broadcast path.
validation.summary: A party that can reach the WebSocket endpoint can occupy a slot and submit syntactically valid opaque frames. The server cannot distinguish a real MeshGram node from an arbitrary client.

dataflow.summary: Signed packet metadata transferId -> attachment filename -> File write.

attackPath.impact: Potential internal file pollution or application storage denial of service.

reachability.summary: Reachable from a malicious MeshGram peer able to send a valid encrypted packet in the scanned snapshot.

confidence.rationale: The snapshot source directly concatenated transferId into a File under attachmentsDir without canonical containment.

findings.remediation: Use a restricted filename token and canonical containment check for every attachment read/write. This remediation is present in the final 1.0.6 worktree and covered by the current build.

rootCause.summary: Remote file metadata was treated as a safe path component without normalization and root containment.

severity.rationale: The path was derived from an encrypted, signed packet but a malicious installed peer could choose its own transfer identifier. The impact is app-private file pollution or denial of service rather than code execution.

findings.summary: The scan snapshot used a remote transfer identifier directly in the attachment filename before writing encrypted data.
findings.title: Incoming transfer metadata could escape the attachment directory

validation.counterevidence_or_proof_gap: The Android app sandbox limits impact to app-accessible storage; the current worktree now sanitizes the token and verifies canonical containment before writing or reading.
validation.method: Source-backed trace from incoming file chunk metadata to saveAttachment.
validation.summary: A malicious peer could choose transferId values containing path separators in the pre-fix snapshot, reaching the local file write operation.
